bug_semantics: ERC7984's encrypted uint64 total-supply update deliberately turns an overflowing mint into a zero transfer rather than reverting. ERC7984ERC20Wrapper's wrap and ERC-1363 callback paths transfer or have already received the underlying ERC-20 before calling _mint, ignore _mint's returned transferred amount, and still complete. Once confidential total supply is full, a user therefore pays underlying tokens but receives no wrapped confidential tokens.
flaw_origin: The wrapper's incorrect success assumption originated in the first decomposed member of squash PR #11: it introduced both wrapper entry paths with an unchecked _mint after underlying custody had moved. The base token's pre-existing _update/tryIncrease contract already exposed failure through a zero return, so the wrapper caller—not the saturating encrypted arithmetic—introduced the loss-of-funds composition flaw.
ai_marker: absent: raw BIC commit object 58f350da0359bc8de8d6a0a97e9ea35b664b44be has human author and committer Hadrien Croubois <hadrien.croubois@gmail.com>, subject 'Add Confidential wrapper for ERC20 tokens', no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, and no bot identity or AI marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-confidential-contracts/security/advisories/GHSA-hqf9-8xv5-x8xw states <=0.3.0 is affected and 0.3.1 is patched, explaining that euint64 total-supply overflow makes _mint fail silently while wrap/onTransferReceived do not check its result. PR #11's first-party commits API lists six members; local git show of 58f350da0359bc8de8d6a0a97e9ea35b664b44be shows it created contracts/token/extensions/ConfidentialFungibleTokenERC20Wrapper.sol. At BIC lines 41 and 46-47, onTransferReceived calls _mint without its return and wrap calls safeTransferFrom before an unchecked _mint. In the same BIC tree, contracts/token/ConfidentialFungibleToken.sol:205 calls tryIncrease(_totalSupply, amount), and line 215 selects amount or encrypted zero into transferred. Later member e2adee4c7dee6a214fb10194daf0133d88bf8312 corrected imports/value/rate details but retained both flawed paths, so it was not the first writer. Direct parent check `git ls-tree -r e1516e341eaae579028ab3b61523ef4d606457bc -- contracts/token/extensions/ConfidentialFungibleTokenERC20Wrapper.sol` returned no entry, while the parent-to-BIC diff reported status A. The final member 214750ca57768e2ad8e22b05658d2f0e8517421a and landed squash cb6a8a7bcc27352530164817c8b68333336f22c3 have the identical wrapper blob ee62576997e35beaa7112a0a03d8d5c08bffc657, proving decomposition linkage. `git tag --contains cb6a8a7...` includes v0.1.0, v0.2.0 and vulnerable boundary v0.3.0. Release-branch fix c620d4386021dde63ae3ea1507dee8543791134a (https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-confidential-contracts/commit/c620d4386021dde63ae3ea1507dee8543791134a) has v0.3.0 commit f0914b66f9f3766915403587b1ef1432d53054d3 as parent, adds ERC7984TotalSupplyOverflow and an _update mint guard based on underlying balance/rate, and is contained by v0.3.1 and v0.3.2. Original upstream fix 2484df01ca18fd5143dae744f46aac0bf8a2b43b has the identical fixed wrapper blob 833f124cad6087c1633013d88efe483614c14ef2 and is contained by v0.4.0 and later tags. `git cat-file commit 58f350da...` supplies the BIC-only attribution check stated in ai_marker.
reasoning: The lifecycle begins with decomposed PR #11 member 58f350da0359bc8de8d6a0a97e9ea35b664b44be, not its later squash carrier cb6a8a7bcc27352530164817c8b68333336f22c3. Its parent lacks the wrapper entirely, and the BIC first combines irreversible-in-the-successful-transaction underlying custody with an ignored mint result. ERC7984's encrypted arithmetic cannot synchronously branch on overflow by reverting and instead returns encrypted zero, so a full wrapper leaves underlying assets in the contract without issuing the corresponding claim. Subsequent PR members only made the initial wrapper compile, adjusted conversion math, tested, and polished it; the final member's wrapper blob exactly equals the landed squash blob. That carrier shipped by v0.1.0 and remains ancestral to v0.3.0. The v0.3 release-line patch c620d4386021dde63ae3ea1507dee8543791134a detects an inferred supply beyond uint64 capacity and reverts from the mint update; transaction atomicity then rolls back the underlying transfer/callback, closing the loss path in v0.3.1. Because the raw commit object of the smallest BIC names only a human author/committer and contains no AI attribution trailer or bot marker, later repository AI markers are irrelevant under the BIC-only rule and the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
